Priya (PM): Quick sync — ACME pilot: they say per-tenant routing + per-route SLO controls are non-negotiable. We need to decide parity vs pragmatic ship. :sparkles:
Alex (Eng): Understood. Full parity equals: per-tenant policy engine, per-route override table, UI + control-plane validators. Ballpark: 3–4 eng sprints if we do UI + safe rollout paths.
Maria (Design): We should avoid building a full console first. Suggest a compact pattern  an authoring modal + a single 'routing profile' resource that can be applied to routes. Keep knobs minimal: latency, cost, isolation.
Sam (Sales): ACME will sign the pilot if we commit to a narrow list of routes and a short delivery window. They mostly want guarantees (SLOs) not a polished UX.
Chris (Research): Competitor snapshot: CompetitorQ lets customers set route-level overrides and traffic weights. Their fallbacks are inconsistent, and their telemetry is opaque. If we focus on clear fallback semantics and measurable SLO reporting, that's a differentiator.
Alex (Eng): Technical options: (1) Minimal parity shim: map tenant-level settings to existing routing policy layer + explicit fallback to compatible model variants. No canary percentages initially. (2) Full parity: add dynamic traffic split and canary percents + console flows. (1) is 68 weeks for pilot-ready; (2) ~3 months.
Priya (PM): Proposal: two-phase plan. Phase 1 (pilot-ready, 68w): routing profiles, explicit deterministic fallback behavior, API hooks, basic telemetry. Phase 2 (post-pilot, 12w): add traffic-split/canary percentages, console UX, rollout telemetry, SLA automation. Vote?
Maria (Design): For Phase 1 I can deliver a minimal modal and small table using existing components. UX scope: 1 modal, 1 table, 1 confirmation flow. That keeps dev work focused.
Sam (Sales): I'll push ACME to accept Phase 1 as the pilot scope and get a committed prepayment. They prefer that to waiting for full parity. We should document no SLA escalation until Phase 2 is done.
Chris (Research): I can attach an eval harness for the pilot to detect output regressions vs baseline prompts. Recommend pre-commit regression alerts tied to their prompt set.
Alex (Eng): OpsBot: note: current routing infra at west-1 has ~30% spare capacity during normal traffic. If ACME spikes, fallback plan = route to hosted LZ in eu-west + throttle at ingress. Recommend autoscale rule + immediate fallback route configured.
Priya (PM): Action items: Alex -> scope minimal parity API + infra ticket list (due EOW). Maria -> Phase 1 mock (handoff in 5 days). Chris -> eval harness + alerts. Sam -> close pilot contract terms by next Wed. I'll draft go/no-go criteria for pilot start.
Alex (Eng): One dev caveat: dynamic canaries require changes to routing control-plane state and rollout service; if blocked we scope-cut console and canaries to Phase 2.
Maria (Design): Aiming for a clickable prototype by Monday for Phase 1 flows. Will keep copy terse and show error states.
Sam (Sales): I'll send ACME the Phase 1 scope doc and payment term sheet today.
Priya (PM): Great. Review meeting Tues 10am to reconcile scope vs risk. @Alex @Sam please align on exact fallback semantics before then.
OpsBot: Created tickets INF-8273 (routing-profiles), UI-445 (routing-modal), TELE-221 (pilot telemetry), and linked to pilot epic EPIC-914.
